A 41-year-old male is brought to the emergency department by his wife due to increased somnolence.
His medical history includes congestive heart failure, diabetes, and hypertension. His vital signs show:

temperature 97.2°F (37.5°C), blood pressure 106/51 mmHg, heart rate 40/min, respiratory rate 15/min,
and oxygen saturation 95% on room air. Physical examination reveals wheezing. Laboratory studies
demonstrate a blood glucose of 47 mg/dL and elevated potassium levels. What is the most appropriate
therapeutic intervention for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Sodium bicarbonate (B) Atropine (C)
Calcium chloride (D) Regular insulin alone (E) Glucagon (F) Octreotide (G) Albuterol nebulizer (H)
Diazoxide (I) Calcium gluconate (J) Dextrose
 A. Octreotide
B. Sodium bicarbonate
C. Calcium gluconate
D. Calcium chloride
E. Albuterol nebulizer
F. Regular insulin alone
G. Glucagon
H. Atropine
I. Diazoxide
J. Dextrose
